subject.title: fix(sessions): cap in-memory session history to prevent unbounded growth

question: Should this PR land as a steady-state retained-history fix while unpaginated initial load and refresh may still materialize the full existing transcript?
rationale: Source inspection shows the patch solves resident append growth but may not bound peak memory, so the accepted scope of the availability fix requires Gateway owner intent.

options.title: Bound reads before merge
options.body: Use a bounded tail-reader path for unpaginated initial load and refresh so both peak and retained memory are constrained.

options.title: Track peak memory separately
options.body: Merge the focused retained-state cap after proof and open a narrow follow-up for full-read peak-memory behavior.

recommendation.title: Bound reads before merge
recommendation.body: Use a bounded tail-reader path for unpaginated initial load and refresh so both peak and retained memory are constrained.

likelyOwner.reason: This contributor's merged work introduced the cursor-pagination and SSE invariants most directly affected by the scope decision.
